plain_english: O Lord, what is the Unsurpassable that grants Kaula fruit by itself — known by a mere touch of knowing, rising to kinship with the Sky-Goer?
sanskrit_cite: anuttaraṃ kathaṃ deva svataḥ kaulikasiddhidam | yena vijñātamātreṇa khecarīsamatāṃ vrajet

plain_english: Tell me this secret of secrets, Lord — the Power that dwells in the heart, Kaulinī, mistress of the clan.
sanskrit_cite: etad guhyaṃ mahāguhyaṃ kathayasva mama prabho | hṛdayasthā tu yā śaktiḥ kaulinī kulanāyikā

plain_english: Tell me of her, Lord of gods, by whom I come to fullness. — Listen, blessed Goddess: even the answer has one beyond it — the Unsurpassable.
sanskrit_cite: tām me kathaya deveśa yena tṛptiṃ vrajāmy aham | śṛṇu devi mahābhage uttarasyāpy anuttaram

plain_english: I tell it, no doubt: swift Kaula-fruition. This Kaula rite, Goddess, abides in my heart-sky.
sanskrit_cite: kathayāmi na saṃdehaḥ sadyaḥ kaulikasiddhidam | kauliko 'yaṃ vidhir devi mama hṛdvyomny avasthitaḥ

plain_english: First now: all lunar days, vowels ending in the drop; within them, by time's conjoining, moon and sun are declared.
sanskrit_cite: athādyās tithayaḥ sarve svarā bindvavasānakāḥ | tadantaḥ kālayogena somasūryau prakīrtitau

plain_english: Realities from earth to person, in five groups in order — in the ka-series and the rest, ending with the ma-sound, O fair-vowed one.
sanskrit_cite: pṛthivyādīni tattvāni puruṣāntāni pañcasu | kramāt kādiṣu vargeṣu makārānteṣu suvrate

plain_english: Fourfold the stations of wind, fire, water and their lords; above them the famous śa-series, and before, the five Brahmas.
sanskrit_cite: vāyvagnisalilendrāṇāṃ dhāraṇānāṃ catuṣṭayam | tadūrdhve śādivikhyātam purastād brahmapañcakam

plain_english: Rootless, in due order, to be known, ending in kṣa — this forthgoing declared; of all mantras and wisdoms indeed, O glorious one.
sanskrit_cite: amūlā tatkramā jñeyā kṣāntā sṛṣṭir udāhṛtā | sarveṣāṃ caiva mantrāṇāṃ vidyānāṃ ca yaśasvini

plain_english: This is the womb, ever told in all Tantras — joined with the fourteen and the tithi-lord's end; the third brahma, fair-hipped, the heart of Bhairava himself.
sanskrit_cite: iyaṃ yoniḥ samākhyātā sarvatantreṣu sarvadā | caturdaśayutaṃ bhadre tithīśāntasamanvitam | tṛtīyam brahma suśroṇi hṛdayam bhairavātmanaḥ
